results.title: Finite retained interior staircase certificate
claims: On one retained vector of coordinate-separable AND routes, m positive staircase sites and m-1 negative connectors force at least m total routes.

For exactly m independent iid routes with null axis mass, certificate probability is m! product mu(B_i); independent heterogeneous laws instead yield a permanent. The stipulated full-support Joe alternative gives positive mass, while n=m-1 routes cannot realize the event, hence finite-panel forward KL is infinite.
The n=1 certificate probability is 10/3 - 8 sqrt(14)/9. A certificate-only waiting rule has mean at least m^m/m! in the iid case.

results.title: Exact two-dimensional minimal panel and bounded adaptive support
claims: For a consistent finite 2D panel, the least route count is 0 with no positives and otherwise 1+tau, where tau hits the negative-obligation cut intervals on the minimal positive antichain.
Forcing m routes needs at least m positive and m-1 negative probes; strict interior staircases attain 2m-1.

For any common measurable threshold-independent randomized policy of depth <=2n, any nonempty finite source inventory with thresholds in (0,1]^2 has transcript law absolutely continuous with respect to an n-route independent open-square-full-support target. Thus 2n+1 is the sharp one-sided support-separation depth under the stated 2D laws.
In 3D four probes force three routes, refuting unrestricted extension of the 2D 2m-1 bound.
limits: Zero-coordinate source thresholds and empty source inventories are excluded from adaptive transport; upper-boundary atoms are allowed. The deterministic formula separately allows thresholds in [0,1]^2.
Seed law must be common and independent of vector; measurability required. Support inclusion alone implies neither finite KL nor bounded likelihood or sample-rate/stopping guarantees.
No new Lean proof; finite grids and seeded synthetic 4x4 controls do not test all real policies or supply empirical data.
